description: Web Audio sound engine + testable pure helpers, wired to game event moments (feed, train, battle hit, win, lose/draw, evolution). Autoplay-policy compliant: no audio before first user gesture. Pure logic (event->tone config, volume clamp, enabled gating) lives in ui-helpers.ts with unit tests; the AudioContext/Oscillator side lives in a new sound.ts module and is NOT unit-tested (documented).
steps: In packages/frontend/src/ui-helpers.ts, add pure, DOM/React-free helpers MIRRORING the existing CARE_EFFECTS/careEffect pattern (lines ~420-448): (a) a `SoundEvent` union type `"feed" | "train" | "hit" | "win" | "lose" | "draw" | "evolve"`; (b) a `SoundTone` interface describing a short synthesized blip (e.g. { freq: number, durationMs: number, type: OscillatorType, gain: number } or a small array of such steps for a 2-note jingle on win/evolve); (c) a `SOUND_TONES: Record<SoundEvent, SoundTone | SoundTone[]>` map with short non-annoying values (keep durations <= ~250ms per blip, win/evolve may be a 2-3 note arpeggio); (d) `soundTone(event: SoundEvent)` accessor; (e) `clampVolume(v: number): number` returning Math.max(0, Math.min(1, v)) with NaN guarded to a default; (f) `shouldPlaySound(enabled: boolean, volume: number): boolean` returning enabled && clampVolume(volume) > 0 (the enabled-gating helper). Keep JSDoc explaining these are the testable pure parts and that the AudioContext side is in sound.ts and intentionally untested.

Create packages/frontend/src/sound.ts: a small module exposing a sound engine. Lazily create a single AudioContext ONLY on first user gesture (do not construct it at module load / import time). Export something like `playSound(event: SoundEvent, opts: { enabled: boolean; volume: number }): void` that: returns early if `!shouldPlaySound(enabled, volume)`; lazily creates/resumes the AudioContext (calling resume() to satisfy autoplay policy); builds OscillatorNode + GainNode from `soundTone(event)` (clampVolume(volume) scales the gain), schedules a short envelope (quick attack + decay to avoid clicks), starts and stops the oscillator(s). Guard the whole thing in try/catch and no-op when `typeof window === 'undefined'` or AudioContext is unavailable so it never throws. Add a top-of-file JSDoc stating: AUTOPLAY POLICY = the AudioContext is created/resumed only inside playSound which is only ever called from user-gesture-driven event handlers, and nothing plays until the user has enabled SFX AND volume > 0; this module is the browser/DOM side and is deliberately not unit-tested (the pure logic it depends on lives in ui-helpers.ts and IS tested).

Decide and DOCUMENT the autoplay approach as: default SFX ENABLED=false (muted) persisted in settings (coordinated with FEAT-003's settings default), so even the first gesture plays nothing until the user turns SFX on; AND the AudioContext is only ever created/resumed inside playSound. State this in the sound.ts JSDoc. (FEAT-003 owns the actual settings state/persistence; FEAT-002 just consumes an {enabled, volume} passed from App.)

Wire event moments in packages/frontend/src/App.tsx so each plays the matching SFX. App must read the current SFX settings (enabled + volume). Since FEAT-003 introduces the settings state, FEAT-002 may introduce a minimal interim source (e.g. read from a settings helper that FEAT-003 will formalize) OR coordinate ordering - but at minimum: in triggerCareFx, play `feed` for feed and `train` for train (do NOT play for sleep/wake/clean/pet unless trivially mapped - the issue scope is feed+train+battle+evolution; keep clean/sleep/pet silent to match the issue). Call playSound inside the care handlers which are already user-gesture driven.

Battle hit + result SFX: in packages/frontend/src/components/BattlePanel.tsx, the per-turn `play()` function is the hit moment -> play `hit`; when the winner headline is set (end of replay) -> play `win`/`lose`/`draw` based on result.winner. BattlePanel must receive the SFX settings (enabled+volume) via props from App (pass through like other props). NOTE: the battle replay runs on a setInterval AFTER the user clicked Fight; this is still within an interaction-initiated flow and the AudioContext will already have been resumed by the Fight click, so it is autoplay-compliant. Ensure the very first gesture (the Fight click) resumes the context.

Evolution SFX: play `evolve` when the EvolutionBanner appears, i.e. when game.justEvolvedTo transitions from null to a stage. Trigger this in App.tsx via a useEffect keyed on game.justEvolvedTo (play when it becomes non-null). NOTE autoplay: evolution can occur from a background TIME_TICK with no immediate gesture; the AudioContext may be suspended. This is acceptable because by default SFX is muted; once the user has enabled SFX they will already have interacted (toggling the setting is itself a gesture that can resume the context). Document this reasoning in a code comment. Do not throw if the context is suspended - playSound guards it.

Add unit tests to packages/frontend/src/game-ui.test.ts for the NEW pure helpers only (import them at the top import block): clampVolume (clamps below 0 to 0, above 1 to 1, NaN to default, passes through mid values); shouldPlaySound (false when !enabled, false when volume 0, true when enabled && volume>0); soundTone/SOUND_TONES (every SoundEvent has a defined tone config; durations are positive and short). Do NOT import sound.ts in tests (it touches AudioContext). Follow the existing node:test / assert style.
acceptance_criteria: No audio can play before a user gesture: playSound only ever creates/resumes the AudioContext internally and is only invoked from gesture-driven handlers; default SFX enabled=false. This is documented in sound.ts.
feed, train, battle hit, win, lose, draw, and evolution each map to a distinct short synthesized tone config in SOUND_TONES; no third-party audio files are added.
ui-helpers.ts exports clampVolume, shouldPlaySound, soundTone (and SoundEvent/SOUND_TONES) with NO DOM/React imports so game-ui.test.ts imports them cleanly.
New unit tests for clampVolume, shouldPlaySound, and the SOUND_TONES map pass; frontend test count increases above 123 and all pass.
`npm run build` passes (tsc typechecks sound.ts + App + BattlePanel wiring).
findings:
Implemented Web Audio SFX. Pure helpers added to ui-helpers.ts after careEffect(): SoundEvent union, SoundTone interface, SOUND_TONES map (feed/train/hit/draw single notes <=250ms; win/evolve 3-note arpeggios, lose 2-note), soundTone() accessor, clampVolume() (NaN/Infinity -> DEFAULT_SOUND_VOLUME=0.5, clamped [0,1]), shouldPlaySound(enabled, volume). New sound.ts holds the lazily-created single AudioContext (built/resumed only inside playSound), per-note OscillatorNode+GainNode with attack/release envelope, guarded by try/catch and typeof window; NOT unit-tested (documented in top JSDoc + ui-helpers comment).

INTERIM SETTINGS SOURCE for FEAT-003 to EXTEND (not duplicate): added to ui-helpers.ts -> interface DisplaySettings {sfxEnabled:boolean; volume:number}, SETTINGS_STORAGE_KEY='ddm.settings', DEFAULT_SETTINGS {sfxEnabled:false, volume:0.5}, DEFAULT_SOUND_VOLUME=0.5, and readSettings() (guarded localStorage read, falls back to DEFAULT_SETTINGS on missing/corrupt). FEAT-003 should build its reactive settings state/persistence on this same key + shape and add reducedMotion/lang fields. Default is MUTED (sfxEnabled=false) to satisfy the autoplay policy.

Wiring: App.tsx reads readSettings() per render (interim; FEAT-003 makes it reactive) and threads {enabled, volume} as sfxEnabled/sfxVolume. triggerCareFx plays feed/train only (clean/sleep/wake/pet stay silent per issue scope); evolve plays via a useEffect keyed on game.justEvolvedTo!==null (background-tick autoplay reasoning documented in a comment). BattlePanel.tsx gained sfxEnabled?/sfxVolume? props (default false/0.5): per-turn play() emits 'hit'; winner set (both the interval end and the no-turns defensive branch) emits win/lose/draw via winnerSound(player->win, enemy->lose, draw->draw). Fight click gesture resumes the context before the setInterval replay.

Tests: added 7 tests to game-ui.test.ts for clampVolume, shouldPlaySound, soundTone/SOUND_TONES (no sound.ts import). Frontend test count 123 -> 130 passing, 0 failing. Shared still 152. npm run build green (tsc typechecks sound.ts + App + BattlePanel). No new runtime deps. i18n untouched (no new strings in FEAT-002; strings come in FEAT-003). README asset-license note is NOT needed since no audio FILES were added (tones are synthesized via Web Audio) — if FEAT-003/README task still wants a note, state that SFX are procedurally generated with Web Audio and ship no third-party assets.
